_comment: Teaching/lore NPC on the actor model (plan-entity-model.md chunk 3a) — formerly a statless model/npc type placed from zone.npcs, now an ordinary actor carrying an interaction block. role creature + speed 0 (PO 2026-07-27, D4): an NPC is an actor that authors no movement, not a kind of its own. Unattackable by two AUTHORED knobs (D5): faction townsfolk (friendlyToPlayers ⇒ player damage skips it) and collisionLayer 97 = PlayerStatic(1) + Viewport(32) + MobStatic(64) — solid and streamed, but deliberately NOT on Action(2), so no aura on either side can target it. interaction.range 2.0 [PLACEHOLDER] is the talk reach and, being the wider of the two (D7), sizes the one sensor — which is also the audience interaction.ambient fans out to. The pre-merge aggroRadius 1.0 stayed as authored but no longer governs anything: under D21 leaving talk range now ENDS a conversation, and 1.0 leaves less standing room than the two bodies take up (L26). experience 0 keeps it off the nameplate path; the health bar is accepted (D3). All values [PLACEHOLDER]. The village hermit: first aid for yourself, then healing for others — and, from level 10, the two beast-handling cooldowns (Calm, CharmBeast) that plan-faction-flips.md shipped without a source. They sit in their own nameless second option; being multi-grant, each renders as its own row labelled from the skill name (D17). ⚑ QUESTS (plan-quests.md C4): the Hermit offers and turns in `village-welcome`. Its three quest nodes sit ABOVE root because L3 demands it — a conditional node below the unconditional one can never be the greeting — so the live quest state IS the greeting whenever there is one, and every quest node carries a row back to root or the teachings become unreachable while a quest runs. The offer and turn-in rows point their `next` at the UNCONDITIONAL root deliberately: a quest row's destination is checked BEFORE the ledger op, so a `next` gated on the state the row is about to create would hide the row from itself. See docs/manual-content-authoring.md § Quests.
name: Hermit

lines: You walk out of here a stranger and you'll walk back in as a story somebody tells. Learn a face or two first.

grants.line: The farmer at the north row, and the crier in the square. Go and be seen by both of them.

lines: The farmer and the crier. Neither of them bites, whatever the crier would have you believe.
So you've met them both. And?

grants.line: Good. That's the whole of it — the village knows your face now. Out there that's worth more than a sharp edge.

lines: Did you break your nose recently? Doesn't look good.

grants.line: Let me show you how to tend to those wounds...
Let me show you how to tend to the wounds of your allies...
Most things that snarl at you would rather not. Let me show you how to ask them to stop.
And if you ask well enough, some of them will walk beside you for a while.
